value.rationale: The classical uniform Sierpiński carpet probability measure has a natural complete Fourier-multiplier spectrum indexed by Z². Finding the first two distinct supremal nonconstant levels and all equality frequencies is not an arbitrary slice: these are the exact norms of carpet convolution on its first two invariant Fourier subspaces, determine sharp mixing/contraction, and show injectivity. New p-adic first-divergence and nonvanishing arguments handle infinitely many frequencies. The third spectral level and unequal weights are not covered.
